---
title: "Week 3 application: resolving a sampled attractor"
subtitle: "From state-space observations to a filtration"
toc: true
---

## Scientific question

At what resolutions does a sampled state-space trajectory support connected,
loop-like or more complicated organisation? A single neighbourhood threshold
cannot answer this robustly because it selects one resolution in advance.

## Observed and constructed objects

The scientific object is a dynamical system. The observed object is a finite
trajectory. The point cloud is formed either from measured state vectors or
from delay coordinates. These are three different objects:

$$
\text{system}\longrightarrow\text{sampled trajectory}
\longrightarrow\text{state-space point cloud}.
$$

The second arrow includes choices of coordinates, standardisation, lag,
embedding dimension and sampling. Week 3 then constructs a Rips filtration
$\{K_\varepsilon\}$ from the chosen metric on the point cloud.

## What the filtration contributes

At very small $\varepsilon$, most sampled states are isolated. As
$\varepsilon$ increases, nearby states connect, cycles may form, and later
simplices may fill them. The filtration retains all these resolutions and the
inclusions between them instead of selecting one threshold.

For a Lorenz-type trajectory, it is tempting to read the two visible lobes as
two components or two holes. That reading is not automatic. Sampling along a
trajectory, metric scaling and transitions between lobes determine which
complexes actually appear.

## Baseline and sensitivity

Compare the filtration with a phase portrait, recurrence plot, nearest-neighbour
spacing and a clustering summary. Repeat after changing sampling density,
coordinate scaling, metric and, when delay coordinates are used, lag and
embedding dimension.

## Interpretation boundary

The filtration describes how one representation connects across resolution.
It does not yet say which features persist, and it does not prove that the
sampled cloud has recovered the topology of an invariant set. Week 4 adds the
homology maps needed to follow classes through the filtration.

::: {.callout-note title="Planned data extension"}
The present example is a conceptual Lorenz route, not a reported empirical
result. A later notebook should compare a deterministic Lorenz trajectory with
a carefully chosen surrogate while holding sample size and preprocessing
fixed.
:::
